attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He agrees with SlateStarCodex here but states the point himself as true.

semantics.note: 'It is true' and 'I do think' are firm, not graded confidence. The hedged InstructGPT part is correctly kept as uncertain and is not scored. The core is a retrospective claim that GPT-3 beats GPT-2 and that correct answers became more likely.

contract.note: The result turns on 'any given example'. Read literally (as worded), it is universal, and matched exceptions make it mixed. Read as a general tendency, it would be supported. The contract says this openly and credits the broad gains, so it is fair, but the reading is the evaluator's, not the speaker's.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed independent study (ICML 2021) before the post. Its GPT-3 175B 8-shot baselines (SST-2 95.6, LAMA 63.8) can be read in the excerpt and beat GPT-2 XL. The AGNews 79.1 figure is not visible in the excerpt. The 2.7B rows are GPT-3 sizes.

GPT-2 XL baselines from the same study and methods. In zero-shot, GPT-2 beats GPT-3 175B on DBPedia (64.3 vs 22.0) and CB (44.6 vs 30.4). These are matched exceptions against a universal reading. Its 8-shot rows also show broad GPT-3 gains.

reviews.rationale: The broad claim holds: under matched few-shot conditions GPT-3 175B clearly beats GPT-2 XL on several tasks (e1 with e2). The literal claim that correctness rose on any given example fails in some matched zero-shot settings, where GPT-2 XL beats GPT-3 on DBPedia and CB. Per the contract, broad gains with such exceptions make the result mixed. The evidence measures greedy-decoding accuracy, not per-example sampling probability.
